explanation: Polygenic inheritance occurs when a single trait is governed by two or more genes with different alleles. In this pattern, each dominant allele has a quantitative and additive effect on the phenotype. This results in continuous variation of the phenotypes within a population, rather than discrete categories. These traits are also typically influenced by the environment. Examples of polygenic traits in humans include skin color, height, and eye color. Disorders known to involve polygenic inheritance include cleft lip, hypertension, diabetes, allergies, and cancer.

questions.q: Which group of human traits and disorders are examples of polygenic inheritance?
opts: Skin color, height, cleft lip, and hypertension.
